name: Electric Assisted Bicycle
description: A device with two or three wheels, a saddle, fully operative pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class I and Class III pedal-assist up to 20 and 28 mph, and Class II motor-propelled up to 20 mph. Defined by O.C.G.A. §40-1-1(15.3) and regulated by §§40-6-300 through 40-6-303, as enacted by HB 454 (2019).
restrictions: Two or three wheels, a saddle, fully operative pedals, and a motor with a power output of no more than 750 watts
Class I assists only while the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class II's motor can propel it alone, up to 20 mph; Class III assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
Has the equipment required of a bicycle, and must be able to disengage the motor when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Class III must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour

Bikes made since January 1, 2020 carry a permanent label, in at least 9-point Arial, stating the class, motor wattage and top assisted speed; anyone who alters one in a way that changes its class must relabel it
Class III riders must be 15 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Class III riders and passengers must wear a bicycle helmet, and a Class III can't be rented to someone without a helmet
Riders and passengers under 16 must wear a bicycle helmet on any class, as on a bicycle
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle
Class I and Class II may use any bicycle or shared-use path bicycles may, unless the local authority or state agency in charge bans them
Class III is kept off bicycle and shared-use paths unless the path runs within or beside a highway or the local authority or state agency in charge allows it
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the local authority or state agency that manages it decides which devices are allowed
Excluded from the definitions of motor vehicle and motor driven cycle: no driver's license, registration or insurance
